target.title: Main theorem
target.label: thm:main
target.body:
\label{thm:main}
There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ and $n_0$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item $\alpha(n)\le C\growth{n}$ for every integer $n\ge n_0$;
    \item the set of integers $n\ge5$ satisfying $\alpha(n)\ge c\growth{n}$ has natural density $1$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently,
\[
  \alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{n})
\]
for almost all positive integers $n$, and, for every sufficiently large $X$,
\[
  \max_{1\le n<X}\alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{X}).
\]

headline.leanStatement:
AntichainOfGivenSize/Model/Theorem.lean:106

theorem alpha_asymptotic_order (hprior : Prior) :
    (∃ c C : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧ ∃ n₀ : ℕ, 5 ≤ n₀ ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
        (alpha n : ℝ) ≤ C * quadraticLogLogScale (n : ℝ)) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun N : ℕ ↦
          (((Finset.Icc 5 N).filter fun n : ℕ ↦
            c * quadraticLogLogScale (n : ℝ) ≤ (alpha n : ℝ)).card : ℝ) / (N : ℝ))
        Filter.atTop (nhds 1) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((Paper.goodInputs c C N).card : ℝ) / (N : ℝ))
        Filter.atTop (nhds 1) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun X : ℝ ↦ ((Paper.realGoodInputs c C X).card : ℝ) / X)
        Filter.atTop (nhds 1)) ∧
    (∃ a A : ℝ, 0 < a ∧ 0 < A ∧ ∃ X₀ : ℝ, 4 < X₀ ∧
      ∀ X : ℝ, X₀ ≤ X →
        a * quadraticLogLogScale X ≤ (Paper.maximumBelow X : ℝ) ∧
        (Paper.maximumBelow X : ℝ) ≤ A * quadraticLogLogScale X)
headline.why:
Read independently, Lean asserts shared positive constants c,C for an eventual upper bound, a density-one lower bound, and simultaneous two-sided density one at both natural and real cutoffs; independent positive constants bound the maximum below every sufficiently large real cutoff. These are all the requested claims.

The definitions preserve the objects and endpoints: generatedIdeal is the union of generator powersets; alpha minimizes the number of generators over arbitrary finite ambient universes. BasicLemmas.lean:88–105 establishes existence and attainment, and AntichainReduction.lean:101 supplies an antichain witness. quadraticLogLogScale uses exactly the paper's base-two logarithms, explicitly stipulated at paper:215. Natural-number binders represent the positive integers used by the paper, whose convention is stated at paper:192. Requiring the existential thresholds to satisfy n₀ ≥ 5 and X₀ > 4 loses no eventual assertion. goodInputs counts precisely 5 ≤ n ≤ N; realGoodInputs uses floor X but divides by X. maximumBelow uses Ico 1 (ceil X), exactly the positive integers strictly below X. Separate extremal constants a,A correctly expand the final Θ assertion. No bound, quantifier, or conclusion is missing.

The only external binder, Prior, is a fieldless proposition with constructor ⟨⟩: a removable modelling artifact, not an additional mathematical assumption. Computational finiteness and decidable-equality instances in the definitions impose no extra input restriction.

Verification evidence was inspected rather than rerun. All 138 SHA-256 entries in checks.json match the current files, and every local Lean source is recorded. The saved lake build --wfail has exit code 0 and a successful completion message without sorry warnings. The saved axiom audit checks all 124 project library modules and reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; this agrees with the separately supplied current headline axiom output. The saved Model/Theorem.lean check has exit code 0 and successful closure results. The source sweep found no proof holes or custom axioms; the three partial definitions belong to audit tooling, outside the mathematical statement and proof dependencies. To reproduce the axiom evidence, run: lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true scripts/CheckAxioms.lean.

The headline is deterministic, so the probability-denotation requirement is not applicable to it. The separate probability corollary is explicitly stated over PMF.uniformOfFinset with the paper's strict good event and exact error bound. This verdict concerns mathematical correspondence, not lifecycle status.

Paper/Results.lean:47 gives the exact dyadic range and 4q²+3, including q=0. Paper.quadraticUpper at :53 supplies the displayed Big-O consequence. This preliminary bound is not needed by the paper's sharp-bound proof.

Paper/Results.lean:43; expanded contract in Paper/UpperParameters.lean:26. Strengthens existential a,b by providing the explicit witnesses 5,3, also obtained in the paper's proof. Retains all sufficiently large B, every integer y, positivity, congruence, and both bounds on the same m.

Paper/UpperConstructionGeometry.lean:120. The position intersection is exactly the addressed old blocks plus the whole pattern universe. Holds for arbitrary pattern families and histories with i inactive; r>0 is established by the paper's sufficiently-large-B parameter choice.

Holds for arbitrary histories with i inactive, including the paper's stages. The update identity discharges monotonicity needed for natural subtraction.

Paper/LiteralUpperParameters.lean:231. Uses the paper's literal floor/ceiling parameters and exact constants 5,3. Bounds every active set and history, including the final matching construction, and also supplies positivity and generator-size bounds.
Paper/DirectReduction.lean:107. Contains positive absolute constants, a uniform threshold, 1≤n'<n, and both inequalities for the same n'.

auditSurface.claims: For K>0, membership in the finite profile-image value set is equivalent to existence of a nonempty family of at most K generators, each of size at most B, over some unrestricted finite ambient universe, generating exactly n subsets.
auditSurface.paperSays: paper/Generating_Antichains_Simplified.tex:980: “\V(B,K):=\{\Phi(\mathcal A): \mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_s),\quad 1\le s\le K,\quad |A_i|\le B\text{ for all }i\}.”
auditSurface.why: The theorem explicitly supplies the representation equivalence. Deduplication and repetition reconcile finite families and indexed tuples without changing ideal cardinality. K>0 is paper-stated, and there is no ambient-size cap.

auditSurface.claims: Every bounded profile assigns multiplicity zero to the empty incidence pattern.
auditSurface.paperSays: paper/Generating_Antichains_Simplified.tex:1012: “Delete ground elements that lie in no generator, and identify the remaining ground set with $[N]$.”
auditSurface.why: This generated proof projection records the paper's normalization. It restricts the internal representation, not the input families; the membership equivalence proves that normalization preserves all relevant attainable values.

auditSurface.claims: In every bounded profile, each generator's total incident multiplicity is at most B.
auditSurface.paperSays: paper/Generating_Antichains_Simplified.tex:980 defines attainable families with “$|A_i|\le B\text{ for all }i$”.
auditSurface.why: Profile load is exactly generator cardinality in the canonical realization. This is the paper's size restriction encoded as a structure field, not an extra balance or intersection condition.

auditSurface.claims: There is one natural threshold B₀ such that every B≥B₀ and every K satisfying 1≤K≤(log₂ B)²/(100 log₂ log₂ B) have at most 2^(B−sqrt B) distinct attainable ideal sizes.
auditSurface.paperSays: paper/Generating_Antichains_Simplified.tex:987: “There exists an absolute integer $B_{\mathrm{cnt}}$ such that, for all integers $B\ge B_{\mathrm{cnt}}$ and $K$ satisfying $1\le K\le\frac{(\log B)^2}{100\log\log B}$, one has $|\V(B,K)|\le2^{B-\sqrt B}$.”
auditSurface.why: The threshold precedes both universal parameters; constants and real exponent are unchanged. The membership theorem establishes the counted object's semantics. Prior has no fields.

auditSurface.claims: There are a positive real constant C and a natural threshold n₀≥5 such that alpha n≤C times the specified scale for every n≥n₀.
auditSurface.paperSays: paper/Generating_Antichains_Simplified.tex:156, thm:main(i): “$\alpha(n)\le C\growth{n}$ for every integer $n\ge n_0$”.
auditSurface.why: This declaration corresponds to the requested main theorem's eventual upper assertion. It should not be mistaken for the stronger all-n≥5 theorem, whose exact counterpart separately exists as Paper.universalUpper_from_five. The threshold restriction is harmless existential normalization.

auditSurface.claims: For some positive c, the number of n in [5,N] satisfying c times the scale≤alpha n, divided by N, tends to one.
auditSurface.paperSays: paper/Generating_Antichains_Simplified.tex:156, thm:main(ii): “the set of integers $n\ge5$ satisfying $\alpha(n)\ge c\growth{n}$ has natural density $1$.”
auditSurface.why: This is the literal natural-density definition for the same set, with the same cutoff and inequality direction. It is not merely an infinitely-often lower bound.

auditSurface.claims: There are positive a,A and a real X₀>4 such that every real X≥X₀ satisfies a times the scale≤maximumBelow X≤A times the scale.
auditSurface.why: maximumBelow uses exactly the strict real cutoff. Paper.maximumBelow_spec also establishes attainment on the nonempty domain, so this is an actual maximum rather than an empty-set default or a maximum over only selected inputs.

auditSurface.claims: Shared positive c,C give an eventual universal upper bound, density-one lower bound, and simultaneous two-sided density one for natural and real cutoffs; separate positive constants give the eventual two-sided order of the maximum below every real cutoff.
auditSurface.paperSays: paper/Generating_Antichains_Simplified.tex:156: “There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ and $n_0$ such that” the universal upper and density-one lower assertions hold; “Consequently, $\alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{n})$ for almost all positive integers $n$” and “$\max_{1\le n<X}\alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{X})$.”

rows.label: There exist absolute C > 0 and an integer n_0 such that alpha(n) <= C f(n) for every integer n >= n_0.
For an absolute c > 0, the integers n >= 5 with c f(n) <= alpha(n) have natural density 1; c is chosen independently of all n and cutoffs.
For fixed positive absolute c and C, the simultaneous inequalities c f(n) <= alpha(n) <= C f(n) hold on a set of positive integers of natural density 1.
There exist a,A > 0 and X_0 > 4 such that a f(X) <= max_{1<=n<X} alpha(n) <= A f(X) for every real X >= X_0.
For X >= 0, realGoodInputs c C X consists exactly of the integers n with 5 <= n <= X satisfying both non-strict bounds.
A density-zero count of orderExceptions is equivalent to the density-one goodInputs proportion, and the natural-cutoff good proportion gives the same real-cutoff proportion.
For X > 1, maximumBelow X is the maximum of alpha(n) over exactly the positive integers n < X.
